cards.front: Why do special laws apply to every North Carolina driver under eighteen?
cards.back: Every driver under eighteen is a provisional licensee, and special laws apply because this group has a much higher crash rate.

cards.front: Who may hold a Level One Limited Learner Permit?
cards.back: The Level One Limited Learner Permit is for North Carolina residents at least fifteen but under eighteen who will drive vehicles needing a Class C license.

cards.front: What certificate must a teen show before taking the permit test?
cards.back: Before taking the permit test, a teen must show a certificate for an approved driver education course with at least thirty hours in the classroom and six hours behind the wheel.

cards.front: Before testing for a permit or a license, what must a driver under eighteen show?
cards.back: A driver under eighteen must show the driver education certificate, at least thirty classroom hours and six behind-the-wheel hours, before testing for either a learner permit or a license.

cards.front: Which tests must a Level One applicant pass?
cards.back: A Level One applicant must pass the written, sign and vision tests.

cards.front: Whose signature does a minor need for a permit or license?
cards.back: A parent or legal guardian must sign for a minor's permit or license.

decks.module: Level One rules on the road

cards.front: Who may serve as a Level One supervising driver?
cards.back: A supervising driver must be a parent, grandparent or guardian, or a responsible adult the parent or guardian approves, and must hold a valid license that has been held for at least five years.

cards.front: During the first six months of Level One, when and how may the teen drive?
cards.back: For the first six months, a Level One permit holder may drive only from five a.m. to nine p.m., and only with the supervising driver.

cards.front: What changes for a Level One holder after six months?
cards.back: Once six months have passed since Level One was issued, the holder may drive at any hour, still with a supervising driver.

cards.front: How do the two Level One time phases differ, and what stays the same?
cards.back: Level One has two time phases: in the first six months driving is limited to five a.m. to nine p.m., and after that any hour is allowed, but a supervising driver is required in both phases.

cards.front: At Level One, who must buckle up and who may sit in front?
cards.back: With a Level One permit, every passenger must wear a seat belt or ride in a child safety seat, and only the driver and the supervising driver may sit in front.

cards.front: Which level has the rule that only the driver and supervising driver sit in front?
cards.back: The front-seat rule belongs to Level One: only the driver and the supervising driver may sit in front.

cards.front: May a Level One driver use a cell phone or connected phone technology while driving?
cards.back: A Level One driver may not use a cell phone or any connected cell-phone technology while driving on a public street, highway or public vehicular area.

cards.front: Which calls are the only cell phone exception for a teen driver?
cards.back: The only cell phone exception for a teen driver is an emergency call to an emergency operator, a hospital, doctor's office or clinic, an ambulance service, a fire department, a law enforcement agency, or a parent, legal guardian or spouse.

cards.front: How long must a teen keep the Level One permit before applying for Level Two?
cards.back: A teen must keep the Level One permit for nine months before applying for the Limited Provisional License.

cards.front: How many hours must the Level One driving log record, and how many at night?
cards.back: The Level One driving log must record at least sixty hours behind the wheel, with at least ten of those hours at night.

cards.front: For the driving log, what counts as daytime driving and what counts as night driving?
cards.back: For the log, daytime driving means sunrise to sunset while there is daylight, and night driving means after sunset when there is no daylight.
cards.memory_hook: daylight is day, dark is night

cards.front: Who signs the driving log, and when is it turned in?
cards.back: The supervising driver signs the driving log, and it is turned in to the Division when the teen applies for the Limited Provisional License.

cards.front: How is the Level One holding period different from the driving log requirement?
cards.back: The Level One holding period is nine months, while the driving log needs at least sixty hours with ten at night; these are different requirements that both apply before Level Two.

cards.front: What record must a teen have before moving up to Level Two?
cards.back: To move up to Level Two, the teen must have had no moving violation, seat belt or cell phone convictions during the previous six months.

cards.front: Who may hold a Level Two Limited Provisional License?
cards.back: The Level Two Limited Provisional License is for drivers at least sixteen but under eighteen.

cards.front: When may a Level Two driver drive alone?
cards.back: A Level Two driver may drive alone from five a.m. to nine p.m., and at any hour when going straight to or from work or a volunteer fire, rescue or emergency medical service they belong to.

cards.front: Which level is the first that allows driving without a supervisor?
cards.back: Level Two is the first level that allows driving alone, and only from five a.m. to nine p.m. or when going straight to or from work or a volunteer emergency service.

cards.front: At Level Two, who must buckle up, and where does a required supervisor sit?
cards.back: At Level Two, all passengers must be belted or in a child safety seat, and when supervision is required the supervising driver sits beside the driver.

cards.front: Driving unsupervised at Level Two, how many under-twenty-one passengers from outside the household may ride along?
cards.back: Driving unsupervised at Level Two, a teen may carry only one passenger under twenty-one who does not live in the same household.

cards.front: When may a Level Two driver carry one more under-twenty-one passenger from outside the household?
cards.back: One additional under-twenty-one passenger from outside the household is allowed only when that passenger is a student being driven directly to or from school.

cards.front: What is the under-twenty-one passenger rule when every passenger lives in the driver's household?
cards.back: If every passenger lives in the driver's household there is no under-twenty-one limit, but under-twenty-one household members may not ride along while under-twenty-one non-household passengers are aboard.

cards.front: Which passengers does the Level Two limit actually count?
cards.back: The Level Two passenger limit counts under-twenty-one passengers from outside the household when driving unsupervised; household members alone have no limit, except they cannot ride with under-twenty-one non-household passengers.

cards.front: Does the cell phone ban continue at Level Two?
cards.back: Level Two drivers face the same cell phone ban and the same short list of emergency-call exceptions as Level One drivers.

cards.front: How long must a teen hold Level Two before applying for the Full Provisional License?
cards.back: A teen must hold the Level Two license for at least six months before applying for the Full Provisional License.

cards.front: Which holding period is shorter, Level One or Level Two?
cards.back: Level Two must be held for at least six months before the Full Provisional License, which is shorter than the nine-month Level One holding period.

cards.front: What record must a driver have before moving up to Level Three?
cards.back: To move up to Level Three, the driver must have had no moving violation, seat belt or cell phone convictions in the previous six months.

cards.front: How can an eligible driver upgrade to Level Three or to a regular Class C at eighteen?
cards.back: An eligible driver can upgrade from Level Two to the Level Three Full Provisional License online, and can upgrade to a regular Class C license online at age eighteen.

cards.front: Which limits does a Full Provisional License drop?
cards.back: A Full Provisional License drops the Level One and Level Two limits on driving hours, supervision and passengers.

cards.front: May a Full Provisional licensee under eighteen use a cell phone while driving?
cards.back: A Full Provisional licensee who is still under eighteen may not use a cell phone while driving, apart from the same emergency calls.

cards.front: Which rule still applies after the Full Provisional License lifts the other limits?
cards.back: The Full Provisional License lifts the hour, supervision and passenger limits, yet a driver under eighteen still may not use a cell phone except for listed emergency calls.

cards.front: What should a new resident aged fifteen to seventeen with an out-of-state permit or license do?
cards.back: A new North Carolina resident aged fifteen to seventeen who holds a permit or license from elsewhere should contact a local driver license office to learn which permit or license they qualify for.

cards.front: How does the DMV treat a provisional licensee's driving record?
cards.back: The DMV watches a provisional licensee's driving record more closely and may contact the driver after certain convictions or crashes.

cards.front: What is the alcohol and drug rule for a provisional licensee, and the penalty?
cards.back: A provisional licensee may not drive after or while consuming any amount of alcohol or drugs, and a conviction brings a one-year license revocation.

cards.front: Is the provisional alcohol rule a blood alcohol limit?
cards.back: For a provisional licensee the alcohol rule is any amount, not a blood alcohol limit, and a conviction means a one-year revocation.

cards.front: Which phone activities are banned for a provisional licensee while driving?
cards.back: A provisional licensee may not use a cellphone, type multiple letters or text to communicate, or read email or text messages while driving.

cards.front: Who must wear a seat belt in a vehicle driven by a provisional licensee?
cards.back: Everyone riding in a moving vehicle driven by a provisional licensee must have a seat belt properly fastened.

cards.front: What school discipline can cost a student the license, and for how long?
cards.back: A student loses their license if suspended from school for more than ten days in a row, or sent to an alternative educational setting for discipline for more than ten days in a row, and the loss lasts twelve months.

cards.front: Is the Lose Control, Lose Your License rule about traffic violations?
cards.back: Lose Control, Lose Your License is about school discipline, more than ten consecutive days of suspension or alternative placement, not about traffic violations.

cards.front: What kinds of safety restrictions can be placed on a license?
cards.back: A license can be restricted for safety, for example to driving only while wearing corrective lenses or only with equipment needed to drive safely.

cards.front: How is a driver treated after going outside a license restriction?
cards.back: A driver who goes outside the limits of a license restriction is treated as driving without a license.

cards.front: Is breaking a license restriction a minor infraction?
cards.back: A license restriction is a limit you must stay within; breaking it is not a minor infraction but counts as driving without a license.

cards.front: What may the DMV do with the documents you bring?
cards.back: The DMV may copy your documents or hold them briefly to check that they are genuine, and it rejects any document that shows alteration.

cards.front: What must a first-time North Carolina applicant prove?
cards.back: A first-time North Carolina applicant must prove full name and date of birth, North Carolina residence address, and a Social Security number or legal presence in the U.S.

cards.front: What insurance proof must a driver license applicant show?
cards.back: Applicants for a driver license must also show proof of vehicle liability insurance.

cards.front: Is a card marked Not for Federal Identification still valid in North Carolina?
cards.back: A North Carolina card marked Not for Federal Identification is still a valid state license, permit or ID.

cards.front: What do Not for Federal Identification card holders need for flights or federal facilities?
cards.back: Beginning May seven, two thousand twenty-five, holders of a Not for Federal Identification card need extra documents to board commercial flights or enter federal facilities, military bases or nuclear power plants that require identification.

recap_hooks.text: Under eighteen means provisional, and the driver education certificate comes before any test.
Level One is for ages fifteen to seventeen, and a parent or guardian signs.

recaps.module: Level One rules on the road

recap_hooks.text: Level One means five to nine for six months, then any hour, always supervised.
Only the driver and supervisor sit in front, and no phone except emergency calls.
Nine months held and sixty logged hours, ten at night, are two separate requirements.
The supervisor signs the log, and six clean months open the door to Level Two.
Level Two is the first solo level, from five to nine or for work and volunteer duty.
Unsupervised, carry one outside rider under twenty-one, plus one more only for school.
Hold Level Two six months with a clean record, then upgrade online.
The full provisional lifts the limits, but under eighteen the phone ban stays.
Not one drop of alcohol or drugs, or lose the license for a year.
Lose control at school, lose your license for twelve months.
Driving outside a restriction counts as driving without a license.
A Not for Federal Identification card is valid in the state, but federal uses need more documents.
